name: Nsongo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919/1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, 2 vols. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.note: No Songo-specific statement. Vol. 1 no. 97 'Songo' has a vocabulary column and addenda (p. 780ff, from a Chapman MS); bibliographic note: 'Koelle likewise is the principal authority for Songo, the dialect of the south-eastern portion of the Kimbundu field'. Only a general orthographic remark for all vocabularies: accent 'is so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable that the accent is only employed when.. on another syllable than the penultimate' — not a Songo description.
Stub; no phonology; only classification notes (H24; possibly closer to Teke per Nurse 2003).

sources.citation: Lima de Sousa, Maria de Fátima, Vatomene Kukanda & Joane Lima Santiago. 2011. A posição lexical do songo dentro do grupo H20 (kimbundu strictu sensu, sama, bolo e songo). PAPIA 21(2): 303-314. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20405902
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. 129-word lexicostatistic comparison of Kisongo (informant Zeferino Santos, born Kirima, Malanje) with Kimbundu, Kisama, Libolo; p. 304 says H22-H24 'nunca foram documentadas'; p. 306: 'com exceção do kimbundu, as línguas pesquisadas, ainda, não têm anotações de tons, pois ainda certos dados mal percebidos deverão ser submetidos a uma análise acústica através do programa PRAAT'; wordlist header 'sem anotação dos tons'. Cites Sousa 2010 mimeo and a UAN doctoral thesis in preparation on Kisongo phonology.

sources.citation: Chatelain, Héli. 1888-89. Kimbundu grammar / Grammatica elementar do Kimbundu ou lingua de Angola. Genebra: Typ. de Charles Schuchardt.
sources.note: Describes Kimbundu (kmb), not Songo: 'Accent: General rule: The accent falls on the penult. Ex.: ngitumáka. Exceptions are due: a) to contraction or abscission.. b) to foreign origin, especially when the accent falls on the antepenult, c) to enclitic monosyllables, which attract the accent to the last syllable of the preceding word' (p. xxi-xxii; Portuguese p. xxiii-xxiv 'O accento tónico recahe sobre a penúltima syllaba'). Intro p. xii lists 'os dialectos.. dos Masongos (Ma-songo)' in a wider Kimbundu group with 'particularidades bem definidas' but gives no Songo data.

sources.citation: Lux, Anton Erwin. 1880. Von Loanda nach Kimbundu: Ergebnisse der Forschungsreise im äquatorialen West-Afrika (1875-1876). Wien: Hölder.
sources.note: Appendix 'Wörterbuch der Sprachen der Bunda-, Massongo- und Bailundo-Neger' and 'Einige Sätze aus der Sprache der Massongos' (Songo wordlist and sentences). No pronunciation or accent note; a few forms carry an acute (e.g. latälu) with no rule stated.

sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund W. 1854. Polyglotta Africana. London: Church Missionary House.
sources.note: '5. Songo' wordlist (informant Musewo alias Toki Petro of Freetown, born Bépunt, sold at Loanda). Koelle's preface defines only 'the common sign for the accent' used on words; no statement about Songo accent placement.

sources.citation: Sousa, Maria de Fátima L. de. 2010. Inquérito linguístico: Anotações sobre a Língua Kisongo H24. Luanda: GELIPOL - Grupo de Estudo/Pesquisa em Línguas e Políticas Linguísticas. Mimeo.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Field questionnaire notes on Kisongo (Bouquiaux & Thomas questionnaire); the 2011 paper's Kisongo data come from it; may contain phonetic observations on prominence.

sources.citation: Lima Angenot, Geralda de, Jacky Maniacky & Everaldo Lins de Santana. 2010. Comparative lexical list of Kisongo, Kimbundu and Chokwe (cited via Ntondo p.c. in Lima de Sousa et al. 2011, note 2); and Maniacky 1997 (cited on p. 305 for Kisongo-Kimbundu-Mbangala lexical similarity).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other first-hand Kisongo data mentioned anywhere; Maniacky (RMCA Tervuren) is a tonologist and any fieldnotes may mark tone/accent.

sources.citation: Pires, Alberto Augusto. 1950. Contos indigenas em dialecto 'songo'. Mensário administrativo 35/36: 51-52; Abreu, Vasco de. 1948. Contos, lendas e proverbios (do posto de Quirima - dialecto songo). Mensário administrativo 13: 25-28.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only published Songo texts (Quirima dialect); Portuguese colonial transcriptions often mark the tonic accent with acute marks, which could give an empirical pattern though not a stated rule.
